speaker: Doctor
text:
I have received your report of neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To understand the severity and location of these symptoms, please describe exactly where the pain radiates and when it started.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Electrolytes and Glucose

REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial blood work and imaging show no abnormalities. Since you have normal results but are experiencing neck pain radiating to your arm along with weakness and tingling, does the pain follow a specific path down your arm, and do you have any history of neck trauma or surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your year-long burning pain, paresthesias, and recent increasing hand weakness, are you experiencing numbness specifically in the thumb, index, and middle fingers, or the ring and little fingers?

Also, have you noticed any stiffness or difficulty releasing objects like a key or a glass with your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The combination of burning pain, paresthesias, weakness in both hands, absent reflexes, and specifically fasciculations is highly suggestive of a motor neuron disease affecting both upper and lower motor neurons. The presence of fasciculations alongside weakness and sensory symptoms in a patient with a long-standing history strongly points towards this diagnosis.
